Impulse Responses and Variance Decompositions of a Stored Model

Source: R/irf.modelfile.R
analysis_of_stored_models.Rd

Impulse response functions and forecast error variance decompositions of a model in an HDF5 file, computed a piece of the chain at a time.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'modelfile'
irf(x, ..., chunk = 100)

# S3 method for class 'modelfile'
fevd(x, ..., chunk = 100)

Arguments

x

an object of class 'modelfile', from read_model_file.

...

arguments of irf.bvarmodel or fevd.bvarmodel, which do the work on each piece.

chunk

how many draws are read at a time. Defaults to 100.

Value

What irf.bvarmodel and fevd.bvarmodel return: an object of class 'bvarirf' or 'bvarfevd'.

Details

Both quantities are sums over the draws: an impulse response is a set of quantiles of the responses of the draws, a variance decomposition their mean. Neither needs the draws together, so the chain is read in pieces of chunk, each piece contributes what it has, and the pieces are put together at the end. What comes out is what the same call on the model in memory gives.

For a variance decomposition the pieces hand back the shares of each of their draws, and the decomposition is summarised once over all of them, so statistic, ci, normalise_gir and max_groups describe the whole chain rather than the piece they were applied to.

An identification given per draw is read at the draw's position in the whole chain: a list of impact matrices is cut to each piece's draws, and an impact function is called with the draw's number in the chain. A piece in which no draw is identified – under type = "sign", or an impact function that declines all of its draws – contributes nothing.

See also

Other model comparison: add_forecast_errors.bvarmodel(), add_forecast_errors.bvecmodel(), add_predictive_loglik.bvarmodel(), add_predictive_loglik.bvecmodel(), add_predictive_loglik.expandingwindow(), aggregate_forecasts(), create_external_forecast(), plot_forecast_errors_by_period(), pool_forecasts(), selection_criteria.bvarmodel(), selection_criteria.bvecmodel()

Examples


data("e1")
e1 <- diff(log(e1)) * 100
model <- create_bvarmodel(e1, p = 2, deterministic = "const",
                          iterations = 100, burnin = 10)
# Number of iterations and burn-in should be much higher.

model <- add_priors(model,
                    coef = list(v_i = 0, v_i_det = 0),
                    sigma = list(df = 1, scale = .0001))
model <- add_posterior_coefficients(add_initial_values(model))

file <- file.path(tempdir(), "bvartools-example-irf.h5")
unlink(file)
write_to_hdf5(model, filename = file)
stored <- read_model_file(file)

ir <- irf(stored, impulse = "invest", response = "income", n_ahead = 5,
          chunk = 25)
shares <- fevd(stored, response = "income", n_ahead = 5, chunk = 25)
